tasks.title: Gateway API: header match + weighted split
tasks.question:
ssh cka03010
In namespace shop-gw a Gateway shop-gw (HTTP, port 80) and Services shop-v1 and shop-v2 exist.
Create an HTTPRoute named shop-route attached to shop-gw for hostname shop.example.com:
- Requests with header x-version: v2 go 100% to shop-v2.
- All other requests are split 80% shop-v1 and 20% shop-v2.
Both Services listen on port 80.
tasks.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace shop-gw --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: cka-demo}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: cka-demo
  listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v1, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "1"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v2, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "2"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Check the Gateway
cmds: kubectl -n shop-gw get gateway shop-gw -o yaml | grep -A3 listeners
steps.why: Route will attach to this.

steps.title: Create the HTTPRoute
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/route.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/route.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Rule 1 has no path, so it also matches path /. With equal paths, Gateway API picks the rule with more header matches. So x-version: v2 requests go 100% to shop-v2.

steps.title: Check
cmds: kubectl -n shop-gw describe httproute shop-route | grep -A20 Rules
steps.why: Both rules stored correctly. Status stays empty. The playground GatewayClass points to a fake controller. So nothing sets Accepted. Check the spec only.

verify: kubectl -n shop-gw get httproute shop-route -o yaml
tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Gateway API; gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io: HTTP traffic splitting / header matching
tasks.beginner: Send testers (header v2) to version 2 and split everyone else 80/20. Words you need: Gateway = the entry point that listens (HTTP port 80); GatewayClass = which controller runs it; HTTPRoute = routing rules attached to a Gateway; parentRefs = which Gateway; backendRefs = which Services get the traffic.

tasks.title: NetworkPolicy pick: AND vs OR trap
tasks.question:
ssh cka03011
Pods labelled app=api in namespace payments must accept traffic ONLY from Pods labelled app=gateway in namespace edge, on TCP port 80. A default deny-ingress policy exists in payments.
Several candidate policies are in /root/netpols-ex/. Apply the single file that meets the requirement with the least privilege. Do not modify any file or existing policy.

steps.title: Read every file carefully
cmds: for f in /root/netpols-ex/*.yaml; do echo "== $f"; cat $f; done
steps.why: for f in ...; do ...; done repeats cat for every file. Each "-" under from: starts a separate OR item. a = OR: every pod in edge, OR app=gateway pods in payments. Alone, podSelector means the policy's own namespace. b = AND + TCP 80. c = right senders but EVERY port. d = all edge pods to all payments pods. b is the only least-privilege match.

steps.title: Apply b
steps.why: One file, no edits.

steps.title: Test allowed and blocked
cmds: kubectl -n edge exec gateway -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments | head -2
kubectl -n edge exec intruder -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments
steps.why: Only the gateway pod gets in. If the intruder is NOT blocked, check the network plugin enforces policies. Run kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep -E 'calico|canal|cilium'.

tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Network Policies (search: behavior of to and from selectors)
tasks.beginner: Pick the rule where namespace AND pod label must both match, on port 80 only. Words you need: least privilege = allow only what is needed, nothing more; AND = both namespace and pod label must match (one list item); OR = either one is enough (two list items).

tasks.title: ClusterIP + headless Service and DNS records
tasks.question:
ssh cka03012
In namespace dns-lab, Deployment catalog (2 replicas, nginx on port 80) exists.
- Expose it with a ClusterIP Service catalog-svc on port 8080 targeting port 80.
- Create a headless Service catalog-headless for the same Pods on port 80.
- From a temporary busybox:1.36 Pod, save the nslookup output of catalog-svc.dns-lab.svc.cluster.local to /root/svc-dns.txt, and of catalog-headless.dns-lab.svc.cluster.local to /root/headless-dns.txt.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace dns-lab --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n dns-lab create deployment catalog --image=nginx:1.27-alpine --replicas=2 --port=80 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
clear

steps.title: ClusterIP Service
cmds: kubectl -n dns-lab rollout status deploy catalog
steps.why: Wait until both pods are Ready (headless DNS lists only Ready pods). port = what clients call (8080); target-port = the container port (80). One virtual IP for both pods.

steps.title: Headless Service
steps.why: clusterIP None = DNS returns pod IPs.

steps.title: Lookups into files
cmds: kubectl -n dns-lab run dnsq --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- nslookup catalog-svc.dns-lab.svc.cluster.local > /root/svc-dns.txt
steps.why: --rm -i prints the output, then deletes the pod. > saves the output into the file. Normal extras: a line pod "dnsq" deleted. Also "*** Can't find ...: No answer" (the empty IPv6 query).

steps.title: Compare
steps.see: Both files start with Server + Address 10.96.0.10:53 = the DNS server (ignore it). Then svc: 1 Address (the Service IP); headless: 2 Addresses (the pod IPs).
steps.why: Headless shows each pod.

tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods (search: headless service A records)
tasks.beginner: Make a normal and a "headless" service and record what DNS answers for each. Words you need: ClusterIP Service = one fixed virtual IP in front of the pods; headless Service (clusterIP: None) = no virtual IP, DNS returns every pod IP; DNS A record = a name → IP answer.

tasks.title: HPA: CPU + memory, scaleUp and scaleDown behavior
tasks.question:
ssh cka03013
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named worker-hpa in namespace metrics-app for Deployment worker:
- min 2, max 6 replicas,
- target 60% average CPU utilisation AND 70% average memory utilisation,
- scale up by at most 2 Pods per 60 seconds,
- scale-down stabilization window of 120 seconds.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace metrics-app --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: worker, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: worker}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: worker}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: worker, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, resources: {requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}}}
EOF
clear

steps.title: Create the HPA
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/hpa.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/hpa.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Two metrics: HPA computes replicas for each and uses the higher. scaleUp policy Pods 2 / 60 s = add at most 2 pods per minute. scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds 120 = look back 2 min before removing pods. It acts on the highest recommendation of the last 2 min.

steps.title: Check
steps.see: cpu: <unknown>/60%, memory: <unknown>/70%   MINPODS 2   MAXPODS 6 (real % instead of <unknown> if metrics-server runs)
steps.why: <unknown> = no metrics (yet); the config is still right.

steps.title: Check deployment followed min
steps.why: HPA raises the Deployment to minReplicas even without metrics (it started with 1).

verify: kubectl -n metrics-app get hpa worker-hpa -o yaml | grep -A12 behavior
tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (search: scaling policies behavior scaleUp)
tasks.beginner: Autoscale on CPU and memory. Add at most 2 pods a minute. Remove pods only after 2 calm minutes. Words you need: HPA = HorizontalPodAutoscaler, adds/removes pods automatically; utilisation = usage ÷ request, in %; stabilization window = how long HPA waits before scaling down.

tasks.title: PriorityClass with preemption policy
tasks.question:
ssh cka03014
Create a PriorityClass named critical-jobs:
- value exactly one less than the highest existing user-defined PriorityClass (ignore system-*),
- preemptionPolicy PreemptLowerPriority, not the global default,
- description "critical batch".
Patch Deployment payments-api in namespace prio to use it, and verify that the running Pods have the new priority value.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace prio --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: batch-low}
value: 100
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: team-a}
value: 3000
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: team-b}
value: 7000
preemptionPolicy: Never
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: payments-api, namespace: prio}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: payments-api}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: payments-api}}
    spec:
      priorityClassName: batch-low
      containers: [{name: c, image: nginx:1.27-alpine}]
EOF
clear

steps.title: Find the highest user value
steps.see: NAME VALUE header, then lowest → highest: batch-low 100, team-a 3000, team-b 7000 (highest = last line)
steps.why: --sort-by sorts ascending. custom-columns prints only name and value. grep -v system- hides the system-* classes.

steps.title: Create critical-jobs = 6999
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: critical-jobs}
value: 6999
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
description: "critical batch"
EOF
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/pc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. PreemptLowerPriority (the default) = may evict lower-priority pods to make room. Do NOT copy Never from team-b.

steps.title: Patch the Deployment
steps.why: Replaces batch-low; changing the pod template starts a rollout.

steps.title: Verify pods
cmds: kubectl -n prio rollout status deploy payments-api
steps.why: Priority is copied into each new pod.

verify: kubectl get pc critical-jobs -o yaml | grep -E "value|preemption|globalDefault"
tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Pod Priority and Preemption (search: preemptionPolicy)
tasks.beginner: Create a priority just under the top one. Allow it to push others out. Give it to a deployment. Words you need: PriorityClass = a named number, higher = scheduled first; preemption = evicting lower-priority pods to make room; globalDefault = the class used by pods that name none.

tasks.title: StorageClass (Retain, expandable) + StatefulSet claims

ssh cka03015
Create a StorageClass named retain-local: provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer, allowVolumeExpansion true. It must NOT be the default.
In namespace cache create a StatefulSet cache (2 replicas, image redis:7-alpine, headless Service cache) with a volumeClaimTemplate named data requesting 100Mi from retain-local, mounted at /data.
keys: sc = retain-local (Retain, WFFC, expandable, not default)

kubectl get deploy -A | grep -q local-path-provisioner || kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner/v0.0.30/deploy/local-path-storage.yaml
kubectl create namespace cache --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

steps.title: Create the StorageClass
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path

EOF
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/sc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/sc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. No default annotation = not default.

steps.title: Create Service + StatefulSet
steps.why: Each replica gets its own PVC, named <template>-<statefulset>-<number> = data-cache-0, data-cache-1.

steps.title: Check
steps.see: cache-0 then cache-1 Running (they start one after another; wait for the redis pull); data-cache-0 / data-cache-1 Bound; RECLAIM Retain
steps.why: PVs keep the Retain policy.

tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes; StatefulSets (search: volumeClaimTemplates)
tasks.beginner: Make a storage type that keeps disks after delete. Make a 2-pod database that gets one disk each. Words you need: StatefulSet = pods with stable names (cache-0, cache-1) and one disk each; headless Service = gives those pods DNS names; volumeClaimTemplates = the PVC pattern copied per pod; reclaimPolicy Retain = keep the disk after its claim is deleted.

tasks.title: Re-bind a Released PV (clear claimRef)
tasks.question:
ssh cka03016
The PostgreSQL data PersistentVolume pg-data-pv still holds data, but it is in Released state after its old claim was deleted.
- Make the PV available again WITHOUT deleting it or its data.
- Create PVC pg-data in namespace postgres (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName manual) that binds to it.
- Deploy /root/pg-deploy.yaml (already uses claim pg-data) and make sure the Pod is Running.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace postgres --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl get pv pg-data-pv >/dev/null 2>&1 || cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: pg-data-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 1Gi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/pg-data, type: DirectoryOrCreate}
  claimRef: {namespace: postgres, name: old-pg-claim, uid: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001}
EOF
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pg-deploy.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: postgres, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: postgres}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: postgres}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
        - {name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD, value: cka}
        - {name: PGDATA, value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata}
        volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data}]
      volumes:
      - {name: data, persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: pg-data}}
EOF
sleep 5
clear

steps.title: See the PV state
steps.why: Released PVs never bind again by themselves.

steps.title: Remove the old claimRef
steps.why: The --type=json patch {"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"} deletes the claimRef field. Or run kubectl edit pv pg-data-pv and delete the claimRef block. Frees the PV; data stays on disk.

steps.title: Check Available
steps.why: Ready for a new claim. Check this first, so you know the patch worked.

steps.title: Create the PVC
cmds:
cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pg-data, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
EOF
steps.why: cat <<'EOF' > /root/pvc.yaml ... EOF starts a "heredoc". It writes every line up to EOF into /root/pvc.yaml. This is the same as pasting into vim. Class + size + mode match the PV.

steps.title: Deploy and check
steps.see: Bound pg-data-pv / Running (ContainerCreating for ~1 min while postgres:17-alpine downloads)
steps.why: Database runs on the old disk.

tasks.docs: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes (search: Retain reclaim policy Released claimRef)
tasks.beginner: An old disk is "locked" to a deleted claim. Unlock it, claim it again, and start the database. Words you need: Released = old claim gone, but the PV is still reserved for it; claimRef = that reservation inside the PV; reclaimPolicy Retain = the disk and data are kept when the claim is deleted.
